source_language_scope: Supplied English records only; no new Greek, Hebrew or critical-apparatus verification.
numbering: Exact original nested chapter/verse order, references and anchors retained. The actual inventory contains 833 units in 36 chapters; continuation units and numeric gaps are recorded in inventory.json.
method: Complete actual source and retained target passages with necessary context were read and every retained explanation reread in the recorded batches. Unsupported source units remain pending with zero completion credit. Earlier completed objects and all unresolved evidence are preserved. Inventory alone earns no review credit. No exhaustive discovery or independent specialist verification is claimed.
completion_definition: Completed means the initial curated cross-reference pass: the source verse and every listed target passage were read in the pinned Saints-Translation English records, and each retained pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean every possible biblical connection has been exhausted, or independent scholarly approval.
canon_policy: Old Testament cross-references exclusively within the Saints Holy Bible 70-book edition: 43 source books in their exact order and divisions; matching targets restricted to its 70 books.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The source names Beseleel son of Ouriou son of Or, whereas Exodus names Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur. Their independent identity equation is not established by this supplied-English review. The completed pair concerns the explicitly located altar in 1 Chronicles 21:29, not this unverified name equation.

source_verse.text: The bronze altar that Beseleel son of Ouriou son of Or had made was there before the Lord’s tent, and Solomon and the assembly sought it out.

target_verses.text: “Behold, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with a divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of work,
to plan and design, to work in gold, silver, bronze, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen,
to work in stone and the woodworking crafts, and to perform every kind of work.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The craftsmanship accounts have differently written names and different maternal descriptions: Dan's daughters here, a widow's son from Naphtali in Kings. No reconciliation or personal identity equation is claimed. The retained same-chapter pair compares the request and the enumerated skills.

He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and timber; to weave in purple, hyacinth blue, fine linen, and scarlet; to engrave engravings and devise every design, whatever you give him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of David my lord, your father.

target_verses.text: King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre,

a widow’s son, and he was from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a Tyrian man, a bronze craftsman, filled with skill, understanding, and knowledge for doing every work in bronze. He was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.
